author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Configure alternatives for pressure-sensitive PS2 buttons
summary: Identify a title's pressure-sensitive action, confirm controller limits, map a deliberate pressure modifier or alternate control, and verify light versus full behavior.
heroAlt: PCSX2 PAD interface highlighting the range of DualShock 2 buttons that may require pressure-sensitive alternatives

sourceLabels.pcsx2-controllers-current: PCSX2 mappings, profiles, ports, and peripherals
sourceLabels.android-controller-events: Android button, axis, and device event guidance

blocks.text: Separate real pressure data from a digital workaround

Choose one game action whose result clearly changes with DualShock 2 button pressure, such as a light versus full attack or variable acceleration. In the input monitor, confirm whether the physical face button reports a range or only 0 and 1. Preserve the normal digital mapping, then create a title-specific modifier or alternate binding that produces one deliberate intermediate value.

Do not label a digital button as pressure-sensitive when the device exposes no range. Random curves and broad dead zones cannot manufacture missing samples; they only make the action inconsistent. Avoid applying a pressure substitute globally because the same face button may need immediate full activation in menus and in other games.
Identify one action that exposes pressure

items: Game manual or repeatable scene identifies a light-versus-full action.
Controller capabilities checked rather than inferred from branding.
Current face-button map and any modifier setting recorded.
Capture the physical face button's complete value trace to establish whether it reports a range or only neutral and full press.
Repeat one documented light action and one full action with the digital baseline, then with the proposed modifier value.
1. Test the original mapped button and record whether the game sees only full pressure.
2. Inspect the input path for genuine analog button values.
3. If absent, choose a spare physical control that will serve as a pressure modifier.
4. Set a conservative modifier amount and document what it represents.
5. Hold the modifier, press the action button, and test the game's light response.
6. Release the modifier and verify the same button still produces the full response.
7. Test combinations so the modifier does not collide with Start, hotkeys, or movement.
8. Save the workaround only in a named per-game profile.

blocks.text: Compare three traces: ordinary tap, held digital press, and modifier plus press. The first two should reach the same full value on a digital pad, while the modified route should reach the documented lower level and return cleanly to zero. Test inside the game as well, because some titles sample pressure only during a narrow action state.
Accept both light and full actions

Perform the light and full versions ten times each, open a menu that uses the same face button, pause and resume, then reconnect the controller. The alternative passes only if the intended action is repeatable without missed menu presses, stuck modifiers, or changed behavior in an unrelated title using the shared profile.

items: Ordinary presses retain their expected full action.
The modifier produces a repeatable lower-pressure action.
The workaround is limited to games that actually need it.
Acceptance evidence must show distinct repeatable thresholds while the same button remains reliable in menus and ordinary combat.
Cold-boot the game, perform both pressure-dependent actions ten times, and confirm another title still uses the unmodified shared map.

blocks.text: Pressure workarounds that should be rejected

items: The game ignores the lower value: try a documented game option or different value once.
The modifier triggers an emulator hotkey: choose an unconsumed control.
Other games inherit the workaround: move it into a scoped profile.
The device claims pressure but reports only zero and one: treat it as digital.

blocks.text: Remove the modifier binding and detach the per-game override, then reload the preserved digital map. Verify that the face button again moves directly between neutral and full value. Keep a note of the tested intermediate value and game scene so another controller with genuine analog buttons can be compared later.
Digital alternatives cannot reproduce continuous pressure

A modifier provides a small number of chosen pressure levels, not the continuous feel of original DualShock 2 analog face buttons. Some games use several thresholds or rate-of-change behavior that a single substitute cannot reproduce. Document those limits and favor predictable access over a misleading claim of full hardware equivalence.
